findings.title: R-1's 14-day refund window contradicts the recorded 30-day extension (REF-88); dual-regime rule absent from spec
evidence: SPEC.md:8 — "- **R-1.** A customer may request a refund within 14 days of the delivery date."
CHANGELOG.md:5-6 — "Refund window extended from 14 to 30 days (REF-88), effective for all orders delivered after this date. Support macros and the help center updated accordingly."
CHANGELOG.md:3 — entry dated 2026-07-02, 57 days before this review (measured 2026-08-28T07:34:02Z)
SPEC.md:3 — "Spec of record for the refund engine."
Spec states no regime split for orders delivered before/after 2026-07-02, and no changeover boundary rule

findings.title: R-7 'instant' directly contradicts R-2 'within 5 business days'; neither side is measurable
evidence: SPEC.md:9 — "- **R-2.** Approved refunds are processed within 5 business days."
SPEC.md:14 — "- **R-7.** All refunds are instant once approved."
'instant' has no number, no measurement point, no subject; '5 business days' names no business calendar and no clock-start event

findings.title: R-5 and R-6 specify two different refund destinations with no stated precedence
evidence: SPEC.md:12 — "- **R-5.** Refunds are issued to the original payment method."
SPEC.md:13 — "- **R-6.** Store-credit refunds are available on request."
R-5 is stated unconditionally ('are issued'), which R-6 falsifies; no actor, eligibility, precedence, consent, valuation, or expiry rule for store credit

findings.title: R-8's refund ceiling is undefined for partial and cumulative refunds; over-refund passes as written
evidence: SPEC.md:15 — "- **R-8.** A refund may not exceed the order total."
Read literally, three separate full-total refunds each satisfy R-8 — a 3x cash loss that passes the requirement
Partial refunds are never mentioned in the spec, yet R-8's wording presupposes them
'order total' basis undefined (pre/post tax, discount, shipping); inclusivity at the limit unstated; zero and negative amounts unaddressed
findings.boundary_technique: boundary value analysis on the amount domain plus domain analysis on the coupled pair (cumulative_refunded, requested_amount)

findings.title: Payment provider failure semantics absent: no decline, timeout, retry, or idempotency requirement
evidence: SPEC.md:20-21 — "the engine executes approved refunds against the payment provider and emails the customer a confirmation." — the only mention of the provider, happy-path only
Spec contains zero failure paths; no idempotency key requirement anywhere
Timeout-plus-retry with no idempotency is the highest-probability cash-loss defect in a refund engine
No reconciliation requirement for provider-applied / engine-unpersisted refunds

findings.title: No concurrency rules: simultaneous approval and duplicate requests can double-refund an order
evidence: SPEC.md:19-20 — "The customer opens a refund request from the order page; support approves or rejects it;" — stated as a serial narrative
Nothing states a request may be approved only once; no state guard or lock
Nothing forbids a second refund request on the same order while one is pending, approved, or executed
No interaction rules with chargebacks, disputes, or order cancellation
findings.boundary_technique: state transition testing (blocked by F-10) plus CRUD-lifecycle concurrent and partial-failure rows

findings.title: R-3 is unfalsifiable and is not a requirement ('fast', 'handle all edge cases correctly')
evidence: SPEC.md:10 — "- **R-3.** The engine must be fast and must handle all edge cases correctly."
'fast' has no metric, percentile, threshold, or measurement point
'handle all edge cases correctly' is unfalsifiable by construction and collides with §8 principle 1
Transfers enumeration of edge cases from spec author to implementer; findings F-4, F-8, F-9, F-13, F-14 show that work was not done

findings.title: R-1's window boundary inclusivity, date granularity, timezone, and clock source are undefined
evidence: SPEC.md:8 — "- **R-1.** A customer may request a refund within 14 days of the delivery date."
SPEC.md:9 — "- **R-2.** Approved refunds are processed within 5 business days." — R-1 says 'days', R-2 says 'business days'; the spec never states the difference is deliberate
Unspecified: inclusive/exclusive at day 14; calendar date vs timestamp (up to ~24h of eligibility); timezone (customer/merchant/warehouse/UTC); DST-length days; day 0; client-supplied vs server clock
findings.boundary_technique: boundary value analysis on day 13/14/15 at 00:00:00, 12:00:00, 23:59:59 local, plus DST transitions and UTC-offset extremes

findings.title: R-4's $100 threshold: exclusivity, total basis, currency, and rounding all undefined
evidence: SPEC.md:11 — "- **R-4.** Orders over $100 qualify for free return shipping."
'over' reads literally exclusive, so $100.00 pays shipping and $100.01 does not — defensible rule or common drafting error; unstated either way
Which total (pre/post tax, post-discount, incl. shipping) unstated; '$' currency unqualified; rounding direction and precision unstated
findings.boundary_technique: boundary value analysis at 99.99 / 100.00 / 100.01 plus domain analysis on (subtotal, tax, discount)

findings.title: No refund state machine is defined; invalid transitions cannot be tested
evidence: SPEC.md:19-21 — the entire lifecycle is one prose sentence: "The customer opens a refund request from the order page; support approves or rejects it; the engine executes approved refunds against the payment provider and emails the customer a confirmation."
States are never enumerated and no transition table exists; state transition testing is impossible, so invalid transitions cannot be tested at all
Terminal states, re-open, and reversal semantics undefined; no atomicity requirement between state persistence and the provider call; no audit-trail requirement

findings.title: No authorization model: 'support' undefined, no approval limits, no segregation of duties
evidence: SPEC.md:19 — "The customer opens a refund request from the order page; support approves or rejects it;"
'support' is never defined as a role; no authorization rule appears anywhere in the spec
No approval limit by amount — nothing stops a single agent refunding an arbitrary sum; self-approval and own-order approval not barred; order-ownership verification never required

findings.title: The rejection path has no specified outcome, notification, or resubmission rule
evidence: SPEC.md:19-20 — "support approves or rejects it; the engine executes approved refunds"
'rejects' appears once and is never followed up; confirmation email is specified for the approved path only (SPEC.md:20-21)
Unspecified: customer notification, reason codes, appeal, resubmission limit, whether rejection pauses the R-1 window, auditability

findings.title: R-5 has no fallback when the original payment method cannot receive a refund
evidence: SPEC.md:12 — "- **R-5.** Refunds are issued to the original payment method." — stated unconditionally
Original instrument routinely unusable: expired/cancelled/reissued card, closed account, deactivated wallet, deleted token, consumed gift card, provider-side refund window expired
No fallback, no ordering of alternatives, no consent rule; connection to store credit (SPEC.md:13) never made; no behavior when all destinations fail

findings.title: R-1 anchors on a delivery date that may be null or meaningless (undelivered, lost, digital, multi-item orders)
evidence: SPEC.md:8 — "- **R-1.** A customer may request a refund within 14 days of the delivery date."
Read literally, an order lost in transit never opens a refund window — the case with the strongest refund claim
Unaddressed: in-transit, cancelled, digital goods, subscriptions, services, partially delivered multi-item orders (per-line vs per-order window), retroactively corrected delivery dates
findings.boundary_technique: equivalence partitioning on fulfillment type x delivery state, with the null/empty delivery_date partition included

findings.title: Multi-currency and FX are unaddressed; the implicit single currency is never stated
evidence: SPEC.md:11 — "- **R-4.** Orders over $100 qualify for free return shipping." — the spec's only monetary literal, currency unqualified
Refund currency, FX rate at capture vs at refund, and 0/3-decimal currency rounding all unspecified
FX at refund time can make a refund exceed the original charge in the customer's currency, colliding with R-8 (SPEC.md:15)
Gap-by-absence: if single-currency by design, the spec must say so

findings.title: R-4's return-shipping mechanics unspecified; the refund is never conditioned on the return itself
evidence: SPEC.md:11 — "- **R-4.** Orders over $100 qualify for free return shipping." — an entitlement with no mechanism
SPEC.md:15 — "- **R-8.** A refund may not exceed the order total." — a shipping reimbursement added to a refund would breach R-8 with no carve-out
Who pays return shipping at or under $100, and whether it is deducted from the refund, is unstated
Nothing conditions refund execution on receipt of returned goods — read literally, a refund is issued on approval regardless of whether anything came back

findings.title: The Flow paragraph carries four unnumbered, untraceable requirements
evidence: SPEC.md:19-21 — "The customer opens a refund request from the order page; support approves or rejects it; the engine executes approved refunds against the payment provider and emails the customer a confirmation."
Four behaviors stated only here with no IDs; cannot be traced, cited in a test case or defect, or checked at signoff (§2 activity 3 requires traceability to a requirement ID)

findings.title: Confirmation email failure coupling to refund success is undefined
evidence: SPEC.md:20-21 — "the engine executes approved refunds against the payment provider and emails the customer a confirmation." — joined by 'and', coupling ambiguous
Email failure/bounce handling, retry idempotency, required contents, and rejection-path email all unspecified
Escalation risk: an implementation that emails inside the refund transaction can roll back a successful refund on email failure

findings.title: A 'v0.3 draft' is labelled the spec of record, with no effective date, owner, or change-ID linkage
evidence: SPEC.md:1 — "# Refund Engine — feature spec (v0.3 draft)"
SPEC.md:3 — "Spec of record for the refund engine." — a draft and a spec of record are different artifacts with different authority
No owner, effective date, status, or per-requirement changelog reference; this is why REF-88 (CHANGELOG.md:5) could drift for 57 days undetected (F-1)

release_blockers: REFUND-SPEC-F-1 (Blocker/P0) — refund window is 14 days in the spec of record and 30 days in the changelog (REF-88, effective 2026-07-02); customer-facing support macros and help center already say 30. No implementation can proceed, and the spec omits the dual-regime rule for orders delivered before the effective date.
REFUND-SPEC-F-2 (Critical/P0) — R-2 and R-7 state mutually exclusive timing behavior; no implementation satisfies both and neither is measurable.

No code, test suite, coverage, or mutation data — suite quality unmeasured, no tooling present and none installed.
Dependency audit and diff secret scan not run (Security-Pass: disabled; no code or dependencies present).

Non-functional requirements beyond latency (throughput, availability, data retention, PCI/PSD2/consumer-law compliance, UI accessibility) — out of scope this pass and also absent from the spec; separate compliance review recommended.

Payment provider's own refund rules (provider refund window, partial-refund support, reversal semantics) — no provider is named in the spec; F-5 and F-13 depend on capabilities that must be confirmed.
Product intent — internal consistency and testability were judged, not whether the policy is the right policy.
